top_strength: The pricing and differentiator block was near-complete and script-accurate: 'pricing is super simple,' $95/mover/hr with best-value day tiers, trip fee, No Worries $2,000 with the 60c/lb competitor contrast, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, no-hidden-fees, and the full clock explanation with a 'does that all make sense?' check — and the quote math was internally correct ($475/hr x 7-8 hrs + $210 travel = $3,535-$4,010). She also opened by asking what the customer's biggest concerns were and followed up on prior bad experiences, drawing out a real story (broken TVs, a mover stepping on her kid) and responding with genuine empathy.
coaching_note: She surfaced the customer's exact agenda in the first two minutes — 'efficiency, timing, handling of furniture, and pricing' — and then never delivered against it. Save Your Ass IS the efficiency-and-price answer, and it was completely absent on a 7-8 hour, $3,500-4,000, 3-story, 140-180 box job. Worse, when the customer handed her a live close ('My daughter is home right now she can do it'), she said 'we can schedule that today,' pivoted into the pricing pitch, and never returned — the walkthrough went unbooked and the customer had to end the call by deferring it herself. Coach the discipline of parking a live buying signal out loud ('perfect, let me lock that in right now, then I'll walk you through pricing') and of routing every named concern back into a script section before moving on.
